title: What were the main findings of WHO's World Malaria Report 2024?

answer:
The World Malaria Report 2024 estimated 263 million malaria cases worldwide in 2023 [1]. It estimated 597,000 malaria deaths worldwide in 2023 [1]. This was about 11 million more cases than in 2022 [1]. Approximately 95% of the deaths occurred in the WHO African Region [1].

An estimated 2.2 billion malaria cases have been averted since 2000 [1]. An estimated 12.7 million malaria deaths have been averted since 2000 [1]. The report covers malaria control and elimination efforts in 83 countries [1]. It introduces a chapter on reaching the populations most vulnerable to malaria [1]. High-risk groups include children under 5, women and girls, Indigenous Peoples, migrants, people with disabilities, and people in remote areas [1].

The report highlights positive trends in the scale-up of effective prevention tools [5]. These tools include new generation nets, the malaria vaccines and seasonal malaria chemoprevention [5]. Increases in cases and deaths from 2021–2022 were mainly due to the malaria situation in Papua New Guinea [4].
